messages:
Ava: FYI - we just got a burst of synthetic canary failures across eu-east monitors. Pager triggered for two routes. Looks like false positives but customer-facing latencies spiked for ~90s.
IncidentBot: [ALERT] synth-canary eu-east route-52 failing (5/5) -- page sent to #eng-oncall
Lena: saw customer reports around 09:12 UTC — some 502s on /v1/generate
Miguel: I'm looking at the relay logs. There's a sudden downstream connection reset to model replicas in eu-east-1b. Could be network flaps.
Samar: checking infra metrics — short blip in the cross-az vpn at 09:11:45, interface flapped then recovered.
Ava: good call. Are the canaries too sensitive? They fired on 10% error rate but lasted <30s.
Kai: canary config: frequency=30s, window=1m, threshold=error_rate>5%, consecutive=3
Miguel: those settings will definitely catch short flaps. For short infra blips we should increase consecutive to 5 or window to 3m.
Lena: customers hit error pages during the window though — each spike reached ~200 users. We should treat as customer-impacting and postmortem, but minimize pager noise going forward.
Ava: agreed. Immediate mitigation: I muted the synthetic monitor for eu-east route-52 for 10m to stop repeated pages while infra stabilizes. (muted by Ava)
Samar: infra team applied a soft fix to VPN routing; packets look stable now. Suggest we change canary thresholds and add a recent-failure supressor.
Kai: proposal: frequency=60s, window=3m, threshold=error_rate>5%, consecutive=4 plus rate-limit on alerts to 1 per 10m per route.
Miguel: also add a sanity-check: if backend error_count spike correlates with vpn interface drops, auto-suppress synth alerts and add an automated incident note.
Ava: +1. Can someone create a dashboard widget that shows synth failures side-by-side with vpn/route metrics? That would speed triage.
Miguel: I'll add a grafana panel. Query: failures by route vs vpn_drop_count in same time window. I'll push a dash and link here once done.
Lena: I'll start a customer-impact thread summarizing affected customers and notify CS for outreach templates.
Kai: small follow-up: we should add a hysteresis to the canary so it requires an absolute minimum failure count (e.g., >3 failures) to avoid firing on tiny-number blips.
Ava: action items:
- Miguel: dashboard & dash link
- Kai: PR to adjust canary config (freq 60s, window 3m, consecutive 4, min_failures 3, alert_rate_limit 10m)
- Samar: follow up on infra hardening and VPN monitoring
- Lena: customer comms + impact list
I'll take responsibility to own the postmortem.
Miguel: linking PR/patch draft: https://repo.internal/redwood/monitors/pulls/328 (WIP)
IncidentBot: Incident created INC-2026-1915000: synth-canary eu-east spike — triage in progress
Ava: If everyone agrees, we'll schedule a quick canary config rollout to staging, run a 1hr soak, then push to prod at 13:00 UTC. Any objections?
Kai: fine by me.
Samar: fine.
Lena: 👍
Ava: OK muting ends at 09:25 UTC; keep eyes on alerts. I'll post the postmortem stub in #postmortems when we have root cause.
Miguel: note for the postmortem — include suggestion to implement multi-signal suppression (network events + synth failures) and add runbook steps for short infra flaps to avoid customer pages.
Ava: thanks all, closing the loop here. Feel free to add threads and I'll stitch into the incident doc.
